purpose: Make repository health, plugin readiness, CI posture, documentation coverage, and rollback safety visible for God Mode development.

publishSafety.mainBranchRule: Main is sacred; ship through checked, reversible changes.
publishSafety.rollbackMinimum: Every meaningful change must identify files changed and the command or commit strategy required to reverse it.

lanes.healthSignal: User-visible behavior, accessibility, cache safety, and shared contract parity.
lanes.securityGate: No secrets, no unsafe runtime side effects, no weakened deployment posture.
lanes.rollbackPlan: Revert app UI, script, styles, service worker, and shared contract changes as one feature slice.

lanes.healthSignal: Cross-platform shared contracts and package APIs remain aligned.
lanes.securityGate: Package changes must not expose credentials or weaken local/runtime boundaries.
lanes.rollbackPlan: Revert package contract or API changes with dependent app changes.

lanes.healthSignal: Plugin manifest, skills, agent files, and bundle checker stay synchronized.
lanes.securityGate: Plugin capabilities must stay explicit and least-privilege.
lanes.rollbackPlan: Remove plugin skill, manifest capability, default prompt, and checker requirements together.

lanes.healthSignal: Architecture, quality, AI policy, module coverage, goals, repos, and agents remain documented.
lanes.securityGate: Docs must not contain secrets, private tokens, or unsafe operational instructions.
lanes.rollbackPlan: Revert documentation contract, index, and linked governance file changes.

lanes.healthSignal: Agent lanes define skill source, autonomy limits, tool boundaries, and validation duties.
lanes.securityGate: Agents must be observable, controllable, and non-destructive by default.
lanes.rollbackPlan: Disable the agent lane by removing skill references and checker requirements.

lanes.healthSignal: The main CI workflow executes quality governance gates.
lanes.securityGate: CI must preserve security, documentation, and rollback checks before release claims.
lanes.rollbackPlan: Remove only the failing new gate after documenting why it is unsafe, then restore coverage with a corrected gate.
